concepts.concept_name: Coffee-Braised Chicken with Melted Cheese Crust
concepts.creative_angle: Coffee as a savory braising liquid, finished with a bubbling cheese crust.
concepts.core_idea: Slow-braise chicken in strong black coffee, then broil under cheese.

existing_culinary_context.relationship: Inherits the wine-braised-chicken template but swaps the acid/sweet braise liquid for coffee's bitter-roast base; departs by capping with a melted-cheese crust rather than a reduction.

ingredient_knowledge.property: mild protein and collagen; collagen converts to gelatin when slow-cooked, giving body. Overcooks to dryness above ~74C internal.
bitter, roasty Maillard compounds (pyrazines); reduces to a glaze without curdling; astringency tightens proteins slightly.
fat + glutamates for umami; melts and browns (Maillard) under direct heat; separates if overheated.

technique_knowledge.principle: low moist heat dissolves collagen into gelatin; keeps chicken juicy. Does NOT brown the surface much.
direct radiant heat browns and bubbles the cheese crust; too long burns milk solids.

innovation_delta.before: Chicken braised in wine/stock, finished plainly.
innovation_delta.after: Chicken braised in reduced black coffee, finished under a melted-cheese crust.

mechanistic_justification.flavor_mechanism: Coffee's roast pyrazines echo the toasted notes wine reduction gives, while cheese glutamates fill the savory gap left by removing stock.
mechanistic_justification.texture_mechanism: Collagen-to-gelatin braise keeps meat succulent; cheese adds a crisp bubbly lid via Maillard.
mechanistic_justification.chemical_or_culinary_basis: Maillard + pyrazine bitterness is a known savory enhancer; remains unproven whether coffee beats stock on preference.

trace.creative_hypothesis: Replace wine/stock with coffee as the braise liquid, then cap with melted cheese for a cafe-inspired comfort dish.

risk_and_constraint.risk: Coffee turns acrid if reduced too hard; cheese scorches under the broiler.
risk_and_constraint.tradeoff: Loses the bright acidity wine gives; trades it for roasty depth.
risk_and_constraint.failure_condition: Braising liquid reduces to a burnt-bitter syrup, or cheese blackens before chicken is hot through.

concepts.creative_angle: Dry coffee rub plus a molten cheese core for a grill-friendly take.
concepts.core_idea: Cube chicken, stuff with cheese, coat in ground coffee rub, grill on skewers.

existing_culinary_context.relationship: Combines the coffee-rub technique from barbecue with the cheese-stuffed poultry idea; formats both on a skewer for grill speed.

ingredient_knowledge.property: acts as a dry rub: bitter + aromatic; burns above medium heat. Use finely ground, not brewed.
inside keeps chicken juicy; melts at ~55C; seals the core so chicken stays moist.
neutral canvas; cubes cook fast on a skewer.

technique_knowledge.principle: surface spice forms a crust via Maillard; no liquid added. Burns if heat is too high.
even surface exposure; fast cook. Core must reach safe temperature without burning the rub.

innovation_delta.before: Chicken grilled plain or with salt-pepper.
innovation_delta.after: Chicken cubes stuffed with cheese and coated in a coffee rub, grilled on skewers.

mechanistic_justification.flavor_mechanism: Coffee crust adds bitter-roast aromatics that contrast the molten cheese's fat-savory core.
mechanistic_justification.texture_mechanism: Cheese core stays molten and moist; rub gives a thin crisp shell.
mechanistic_justification.chemical_or_culinary_basis: Dry spice crusting is a standard barbecue mechanism; cheese melt point is well established. Unproven: whether coffee reads as 'burnt' to some palates.

trace.creative_hypothesis: Treat coffee like a spice rub rather than a liquid, pairing its crust with a cheese core.

risk_and_constraint.risk: Coffee rub burns on the grill before the chicken core is cooked.
risk_and_constraint.tradeoff: Small cubes dry out faster than a braise; less saucy comfort.
risk_and_constraint.failure_condition: Rub is black-bittered while chicken interior is under 74C.

concepts.creative_angle: A coffee-laced cream sauce over chicken and cheese, riffing on carbonara.
concepts.core_idea: Make a coffee-infused cream sauce, toss with chicken and cheese.

existing_culinary_context.relationship: Borrow carbonara's cream+cheese emulsion and lace it with coffee the way cocoa is laced into mole for bitter depth.

ingredient_knowledge.property: reduces into a syrup; a little adds bitter depth, too much curdles cream.
emulsifies with cheese (carbonara base); splits if boiled hard.
pecorino/parmesan give umami and body to the sauce.

technique_knowledge.principle: starch + fat + gentle heat hold a sauce; violent boil breaks it. Off-heat tossing prevents split.
steeping coffee in warm cream extracts bitter notes without brewing harshness.

innovation_delta.after: Cream/cheese sauce infused with a little coffee for bitter depth, over chicken.

mechanistic_justification.flavor_mechanism: Coffee's roast notes deepen a cream/cheese sauce the way cocoa deepens chili.
mechanistic_justification.texture_mechanism: Gentle emulsion keeps the sauce silky; coffee adds no grit if strained.
mechanistic_justification.chemical_or_culinary_basis: Cocoa-in-mole is the direct analogy; emulsions are well understood. Unproven: ideal coffee dose before 'ashtray'.

trace.creative_hypothesis: Infuse the cream sauce with a little coffee to add bitter depth, then combine with chicken and cheese.

risk_and_constraint.risk: Cream splits if boiled, or coffee turns the sauce ashy.
risk_and_constraint.tradeoff: Less bright than lemon/zest carbonara; more bitter.
risk_and_constraint.failure_condition: Sauce breaks into oil/water or tastes of burnt coffee.
